subject: Next steps: Hosted pilot operational checklist + endpoint mapping
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: Hosted pilot operational checklist + endpoint mapping

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great to see the intent and where Finlytics wants to embed summarization and realtime Q&A. Per our conversation, below are the recommended next steps to get a hosted API pilot running quickly and the pieces where we need confirmation from your side: 

1) Quickstart + sandbox access (action: Redwood)
- We’ll provision a sandbox org for Finlytics with two endpoints: /v1/summarize (short form) and /v1/qna (chat-style). Sandbox URL: https://redwood.example/sandbox/finlytics
- Included in the sandbox: API key, 30k token trial budget, and a small sample dataset for integration tests. (Attachment: redwood-hosted-quickstart-guide.pdf)

2) Traffic profile & rate limits (action: Finlytics)
- Please confirm expected peak QPS and average request size (tokens per request). Our recommended starter rate limits for hosted pilots are 20 QPS / endpoint with burst to 60 for short bursts; we can adjust once you provide real numbers.

3) Data residency & security (action: Finlytics)
- You mentioned some PII in user inputs. Can you confirm whether log export is allowed to Redwood for troubleshooting, or if logs must be disabled/filtered? If your security team requires VPC-only traffic or no third-party logging, that may push the pilot toward Private deployment.

4) Canary and rollback plan (action: Redwood + Finlytics)
- We recommend starting with a 5% traffic canary to /v1/summarize for 48 hours, monitor error rate and latency, then step to 25% and 100%. We’ll set automated fallback to a smaller, cheaper model if latency exceeds thresholds.

5) Commercial/legal items (action: Finlytics contracts + Redwood sales)
- I’ll share an editable MSA via DocuSign for a 90-day pilot. If Procurement needs redlines, please loop Contracts. DocuSign link will be posted in a follow-up.

Questions for you now:
- Confirm peak QPS and average tokens per request (even rough numbers help).
- Can your security team accept a hosted pilot with redacted logs, or do they require VPC/Private?
- Who should we loop in on procurement for the MSA?

I’m copying Ben (account lead) and Marissa (solutions engineering) so we can fast-track the sandbox and provide a short config for prefix caching / KV cache suggestions.

Thanks — I’ll queue the sandbox once you confirm the QPS and log policy.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>

Cc: Security Team <security@finlytics.com>, Contracts <contracts@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Hosted pilot operational checklist + endpoint mapping

Lauren —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- Peak profile: during business hours we expect ~25 requests/sec for summarization (average ~220 tokens/request) and ~8 req/sec for the chat Q&A (~450 tokens/request) during the pilot target workload. Night/weekend load is negligible.
- Logs: our security policy requires that PII be stripped before any logs leave our environment. We can accept redacted logs for troubleshooting; full request/response logs cannot be stored off-prem without an Exec sign-off.
- VPC: Security would prefer a Private/VPC deployment for production, but are open to a short hosted pilot if the logs are redacted and data retention is controlled (30 days max).
- Procurement: Contracts will own the MSA; I looped them on this thread.

I’ve attached our security questionnaire which may have additional asks.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Head of Product, Finlytics
samir@finlytics.com
(212) 555-0142

Attachment: Finlytics_Security_Questionnaire.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Contracts <contracts@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Hosted pilot operational checklist + endpoint mapping

Samir —

Appreciate the details — that peak profile is helpful. A few follow-ups and concrete proposals so we can move fast: 

1) Hosted pilot feasibility given your constraints
- Redacted logs + 30 day retention is compatible with our hosted offering for pilots. We’ll implement request-side redaction hooks and only store token-level telemetry (no raw PII). We’ll include a retention clause in the pilot MSA.

2) Rate limits & endpoint config (suggested starter mapping)
- /v1/summarize -> rate limit: 25 QPS, avg 220 tokens; autoscale buffer to 75 QPS for bursts; token cap: 150k tokens/min account-level
- /v1/qna -> rate limit: 10 QPS, avg 450 tokens; autoscale buffer to 30 QPS
- We’ll enable prefix/KV caching on /v1/summarize for repetitive documents — this should cut token cost significantly for your workflows. Marissa will share cache TTL recommendations once sandbox data is available.

3) Performance & fallback
- For the pilot we’ll run the higher-throughput variant of the model to keep latency under 300ms median for summarize and under 500ms for chat. If latency spikes above the SLO, requests will fall back to a cost-optimized variant automatically.

4) Pilot commercial & legal
- I’ve uploaded a short MSA to DocuSign (link: https://app.docusign.com/Finlytics-MSA-2026). It’s for a 90-day pilot with standard liability limits; Contracts can redline.

Next actions I’ll take this morning: provision the sandbox org and issue API keys; Ben will prepare a short traffic test harness you can run against the sandbox. Marissa will attach a one-page cache & batching tune sheet.

If Contracts wants a short technical annex about logging/redaction, Marissa can prep that in ~24 hours.

Best,

Lauren
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

2) Security will review the hosted redaction approach. They’ll start with the questionnaire I attached and will follow up with one technical contact (cc’d).

I’ll get Contracts and Security to review the MSA and the questionnaire this afternoon and come back with any questions. If everything looks OK, we’ll sign and kick off the sandbox test next week.

Samir
